anchors: A pattern must also MISS every other refusal the code can raise.
so a pattern for the inner rule also passes when the wrapper fires
decision: A pytest.raises match= pattern must match its own refusal and no other the code can raise: check it with re.search against every raise message in the module and the layers it calls, anchor an inner rule's pattern against a wrapper that interpolates it, and give a test-raised sentinel a whole-matched sentence.

evidence.text: A scan of one library's suite flagged 42 single-token patterns; recording every refusal message the suite raised (551) showed several patterns, and a new alternation pattern, matching unrelated refusals of the same package. RED arms (opus, haiku) on the pre-edit text both listed the missing neighbour check as a skill gap; GREEN arms on both tiers rejected the loose patterns quoting the new sentence.

reopen_if: pytest changes match= from re.search to a full match, or a shipped tool checks every pattern against the code's refusal set automatically in the gate.
why: match= is re.search, so a word several refusals share passes whichever fires and the test stays green when the code refuses for the wrong reason. The earlier text only said to match the validator's phrase and allowed any substring every arm shares.

anchors: A budget the code spends waiting on a stand-in that must ANSWER is roomy
decision: A budget the code spends waiting on a stand-in that must answer is roomy; only a test expecting expiry keeps a tight one; a pacing TCP stand-in turns Nagle off and the test asserts the outcome class and reported == on-disk bytes, never bytes-within-budget.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for Nagle/NODELAY. GREEN opus and haiku: both fixed the trickle test (Nagle off, outcome plus on-disk bytes) and the 1 s vote budget, and left the expiring-budget control alone, quoting the bullet.

reopen_if: A suite following this still flakes on stand-in timing, or a roomy budget hides a real hang.
why: A 1 s budget let one stall on a loaded host flip an unrelated vote about once in three full runs; with Nagle on, macOS delivered 6 of 18 trickled bytes where Linux and Windows delivered all, costing two red CI rounds.

anchors: with every inherited `GIT_*` variable removed first
RED one arm per sink: in a scratch copy
assert an outcome only the timed wake produces
decision: Three defeater entries: a fresh-home commit test sets GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* in a child env stripped of inherited GIT_* with XDG_CONFIG_HOME under the temp dir; a refused-before-side-effect test asserts every sink, RED one arm per sink; a timed-wake test uses a case only the timeout can wake, asserts an outcome only the timed wake produces, and bounds the untimed-wait arm.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for _AUTHOR_/_COMMITTER_, untimed, every sink. GREEN opus and haiku found each seeded defect; gaps closed (zero-completed outcome, bounded arm, GIT_* strip, untouched defined) and a haiku re-run on the final text applied all three.

reopen_if: A test written to one of these entries still passes against the defect it names.
why: Each passed locally and failed in CI or survived a mutation: a commit test red only on a runner with no identity, a zero-timeout test green while every proxy was banned, an untimed-wait mutant surviving a many-short-items test.

anchors: Bind it and keep it referenced past the count
decision: A leak check after a refused call binds the pytest.raises result and keeps it referenced past the count.

evidence.text: Probe: a function opening a file and raising without close; the unbound pytest.raises form passed, the bound form failed on the leak.

reopen_if: The suite counts resources only with gc and refcount effects excluded some other way.
why: Releasing the exception frees the frames holding the leaked object, refcounting closes it, and the count returns to baseline on leaking code.

anchors: an autouse fixture that isolates the suite by setting the OVERRIDE wins over every test that sets the plain knob itself
is found by every test that counts that search's results
decision: An autouse isolation fixture for an override-plus-fallback lookup points every platform's fallback knob under the temp dir and deletes the override with setenv then delenv; a file it plants to stop an upward search is expected by, or bypassed by name in, every test that counts that search's results.

evidence.text: Probe: a lookup LIB_X_ROOT-or-APPDATA with a test setting APPDATA failed under an override-setting autouse fixture and passed under a fallback-setting one that removed the override with setenv then delenv.

reopen_if: The lookup under test gives the plain knob precedence over the override.
why: A fixture-set override wins over every test that sets the plain knob itself, so those tests fail or pass vacuously, often on one platform only; a planted sentinel is included in every count of that search.

anchors: refuses every input the real tool refuses, with the same usage error and exit
decision: A hand-written fake of a CLI the code shells out to refuses every input the real tool refuses, with the same usage error and exit code; for a tool you own, the fake calls the tool's own validator or one test runs the real tool on a scratch tree.

evidence.text: Contribution report: a fake of an owned CLI accepted an argument value the real tool rejects, all 64 tests passed, and the first real dry run exposed it. RED quote-back on opus and haiku against the pre-edit text answered NONE for argument values and exit codes.

reopen_if: A contract test that runs every fake against its real tool becomes part of the standard harness, making a per-fake rule redundant.
why: A fake more lenient than the tool keeps the suite green on calls production fails with; the existing seam-shape rule covered a callable's keywords and return shape, not a CLI's argument values or exit codes.

anchors: honours the stop condition the real one has
decision: A fake standing in for a waiter, poller or child process honours the stop condition the real one has (the --timeout or deadline the code passes it) and answers with the real tool's timed-out result once that limit is spent.

evidence.text: Contribution report: in a 13-arm mutation battery one arm read as a hang until the fake waiter modelled the real tool's timeout. RED quote-back on opus and haiku against the pre-edit text answered NONE.

reopen_if: Mutation tooling learns to classify an arm that hangs to its timeout as killed, so a hang reads the same as a failing assertion.
why: A fake that ignores the limit turns the mutant removing the code's own stop into a hang until the outer timeout, which reads as neither killed nor survived.
